issue: PMAT-535 (closes forjar#535) — a branch names the ticket its work claims. The branch name is read by gate A for a receipt path, by gate E for a quorum filename and by gate T for a release window, and nothing checked it. PR #532 was pushed from PMAT-520-book-v1.29.0 while every commit said PMAT-531, so a ticket that had already shipped in 1.29.0 was credited to the v1.30.0 window and the ticket that owned the work was invisible to all three gates.

quorum.rounds: one round of three sandboxed agy quorum lanes, dispatched in a single message with --not-before pinned to the dispatch instant and out_dir keyed by ticket AND session id. Each lane got a different brief and all three carried the standing instruction to quote any sentence a reader could check and find false.
quorum.kill_rule: six claims and the standing instruction. THE ARM'S STATED REASON WAS FALSE and its true reason was stronger; two normalisations were missing and each was a FALSE REFUSAL measured against the arm this branch had already committed; one read failed open; five of six cases could not die from deleting the arm; and one sentence of the receipt was false.
refuted_claims: That pmat's CB-2113 and this repository's commit-msg hook both match the Pmat-Ticket LINE wherever it appears. Both ask git: CB-2113 with %(trailers:key=...) and the hook with git interpret-trailers --parse, falling back to grep -qE 'PMAT-[0-9]+|#[0-9]+' over the whole message.

That the arm produces no false refusals. A CRLF commit message left a carriage return glued to the id, and the gate refused a branch whose own commit claimed its ticket while printing that trailer one line below.
That one Pmat-Ticket line names one ticket. 'PMAT-535, PMAT-536' is two claims, and unsplit the first read as 'PMAT-535,' and matched nothing.
That an unreadable history is not a pass. git log with 2>/dev/null and no exit check turned a failed read into 'this branch claims nothing', which the arm skips.
That the six falsification cases each fail if the arm is deleted. Five assert only that a message was NOT printed; measured with the arm cut out, only the two positive cases fail.
That all four new bashrs warnings are artifacts of the multi-line die message. SC2101 fired on a case PATTERN outside the string entirely.

That refusing a misnamed branch closes the misattribution. The window rule reads BRANCH, then TITLE, then BODY, and a branch named fix/ci-lint with a PR titled (PMAT-520) reproduces the whole defect untouched.
That the refusal tells the reader the right thing to do. 'or add a commit that claims <id>' satisfies the gate while leaving the branch misnamed, which is the outcome the arm exists to prevent.
lane_errors: lane 3 could not run git at all: the review repository was a `git clone --shared` whose objects/info/alternates points into the parent repository, outside the sandbox. It marked three of its ten findings UNMEASURED rather than guessing, and still found the receipt's false sentence from the files alone. A sandboxed lane needs a full clone.

systems: Gerrit (Change-Id trailer, enforced by a server-side commit hook)
Kubernetes Prow (release-note and area labels adjudicated by a bot, not by the branch name)
Linux kernel patch conventions (Fixes: and Link: trailers parsed by git itself)
Chef Expeditor (version bump and changelog driven by PR labels on merge)
crux.verdict: accept(every surveyed system binds a change to its work item through a field a tool writes and a tool reads -- a trailer or a label -- and none of them derives that binding from a branch NAME, which is free text a human types once and no tool validates. forjar derives it from the branch name in three gates, so the cheapest correct move is not to stop reading the name but to require the name and the trailer to agree, at the last moment the name can still be changed. Where forjar is WORSE than all four: the check is a client-side pre-push hook, so --no-verify, a clone with no hooks and the GitHub web UI all bypass it, where Gerrit's equivalent runs on the server and cannot be bypassed at all.)

NONE of the eight cases in tests/falsification_a_branch_names_its_own_ticket.rs appears in either list. The vacuity charge was answered by cutting the arm's sixty lines out of the script and re-running the gate, which is the only thing that separates a false-refusal guard from a test that proves nothing.
